children: Tata Steel has approved the sale of its tubes business and its entire stake in Tata Steel Colors to APL Apollo Tubes for a combined consideration of up to ₹28,000 crore, as part of its strategy to unlock value from its downstream portfolio and sharpen its business focus.
The board of Tata Steel, at a meeting on Sunday, approved the transfer of its tubes and pipes manufacturing business to APL Apollo on a slump sale basis for a lump sum consideration of ₹11,700 crore.
Separately, it also approved the sale of its entire 100 per cent equity stake in Tata Steel Colors (TSCL), formerly known as Tata BlueScope Steel, for ₹16,300 crore.

Tata Steel acquired its joint venture partner’s 50 per cent stake in Tata Steel BlueScope Steel for ₹1,100 crore in November 2025. The business became a wholly owned subsidiary of Tata Steel in April 2026, following the necessary statutory approvals, and was subsequently rebranded as Tata Steel Colors.

The two transactions are interlinked, with their closure proposed to take place simultaneously, subject to customary conditions precedent and necessary regulatory approvals. Both transactions are expected to be completed by March 31, 2028, Tata Steel said in a statement on Sunday.

The steel tubes business comprises manufacturing, processing, marketing and distribution operations at Tata Steel’s facilities in Jamshedpur, Hosur, Khopoli and Sahibabad. It also includes certain cold-rolling and surface-coated steel product facilities in Khopoli, along with associated plants and operations.
The business recorded a turnover of about ₹11,375 crore in FY26, accounting for 4.9 per cent of Tata Steel’s consolidated revenue. Its net worth stood at ₹3,274 crore as of March 2026.

Tata Steel Colors was 50 per cent owned directly by Tata Steel, while the remaining stake was held through its subsidiary, Tata Steel Downstream Products. The division reported a turnover of about ₹4,680 crore in FY26. The transaction will result in APL Apollo acquiring full ownership of the company.
Of the ₹16,300-crore consideration for Tata Steel Colors, ₹8,150 crore will be paid directly to Tata Steel, with the remaining ₹8,150 crore going to Tata Steel Downstream Products.

APL Apollo, a listed manufacturer of steel tubes, pipes, metal and colour-coated coils, is expected to leverage its scale, distribution network and product portfolio to support the growth of the acquired businesses.
For Tata Steel, the divestments are aimed at unlocking value from its downstream operations and rationalising its portfolio. The company primarily manufactures and sells steel and steel products.

The proposed deals represent a significant restructuring of Tata Steel’s downstream portfolio, while giving APL Apollo an opportunity to expand its manufacturing footprint and strengthen its presence across the steel tubes and coated products segments.

title: Tata Steel to sell tubes business, Colors stake to APL Apollo for ₹28,000 crore
